title: Living With My Brother's Wife
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Seventeen-year-old Shino Kishibe has lost her parents in an accident and, six months ago, her older brother Taishi. She now lives with his widow Nozomi, a primary school teacher, and the two women with no blood tie slowly learn to rely on each other (Manga UP! blurb via AniList and MU; manga-news review of vol. 1).
life_message: Family can be built from trust and daily care, even without blood ties, and grief is lighter when shared.

content.note: Deaths happen off-page before the story; review calls it less gloomy than it sounds.
Review notes a light flirting thread, no fan service. AniList lists low-rank Yuri; MU lists Age Gap and Student-Adult Relationship (nature to verify).
A colleague of Nozomi's drinks too much (review).
Grief is the core theme (review); MU lists Grief, Depression, Insomnia and Dependency.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts are emotional, settled by talk and small gestures (review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: School and work routines frame a home life the two shape themselves.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Story centres on building a family bond beyond blood (review, blurb).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Shino refuses to treat Nozomi as a substitute mother; they meet as near-equals (review).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern secular household; Taishi remembered in daily routines rather than ritual (review).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Focus on emotional well-being and quality of life (review).

folkways.japan: Shino's reluctance to burden Nozomi reflects the Japanese value of enryo (restraint toward others), described here as context.

delivery.evidence: manga-news review: themes emerge through routines and small gestures, avoiding excessive pathos.
delivery.note: The story shows a bond forming rather than arguing a position.

winners_losers: Shino and Nozomi slowly earn each other's trust; sympathy goes to patience and chosen family.
